---
title: "rename() with a named vector builds an extra-long name"
ref: TDY-07
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "a column `identifier`"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2024)"
---

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

sales <- data.frame(code = 1:2, amount = c(10, 20))
config <- c(id = "code", measure = "amount")
rename(sales, identifier = config["id"])
```
:::

## Why

`config["id"]` is not just `"code"`: it is a vector that keeps its name, `id`. When a named selection receives a vector that is itself named, {tidyselect} combines both names so as to lose nothing, and the column becomes `identifier...id`. Code that then looks for `identifier` does not find it.

## The fix

Extract the bare value with `[[ ]]`, or drop the names with `unname()`.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

rename(sales, identifier = config[["id"]])
rename(sales, identifier = unname(config["id"]))
```
:::
